title: NaN equals NaN, of either sign: in `=`, `IN`, grouping, `DISTINCT`, joins and set operations
description: `'nan' = 'nan'` is true, `<>` false, and `'nan' = -'nan'` true: DuckDB compares doubles with NaN as one value above `+inf`, so the sign of a NaN never splits it. `IN`, `IS DISTINCT FROM`, `list_contains` and `list_position` find NaN; `FLOAT` behaves the same.
`GROUP BY`, `count(DISTINCT …)`, equi-joins and `INTERSECT` put `nan` and `-nan` in one group and match them; `-0.0` and `0.0` group and join together too (R14).
reference: `NAN_IS_NAN` (#89, an override of IEEE equality) for `=`, grouping, `DISTINCT` and joins, with one NaN (`nan_kind: ONE_NAN`); docs/core-semantics.md lists DuckDB as `NAN_IS_NAN`. ST-4 records the gap in Substrait.
